scene: Inferno XIV — Old Man of Crete, cracked statue and infernal rivers
source: Dante, Inferno XIV, Virgil's explanation of the Old Man of Crete
story: Virgil tells Dante about an ancient statue hidden within Mount Ida on Crete, turned toward Rome.
The Old Man's head is gold, arms and breast silver, then brass, with iron below, except the right foot is baked clay.
All parts except the golden head are split by a fissure, and tears drip from the cracks.
The tears collect below and become infernal watercourses, described in connection with Acheron, Styx, Phlegethon and finally Cocytus.
Dante asks why the water is seen here though its source lies elsewhere, and Virgil distinguishes the full geography of Hell from the route Dante has taken.
Virgil also distinguishes Lethe, which Dante will encounter outside Hell; do not merge Lethe into this statue's four-river topology.
The travelers remain at the stream, ready to continue beyond this explanatory encounter.
